David Burton

still a work

Brooklyn guy who shoots film.

I picked up a film camera at my parents' place during the pandemic and have slowly used it more and more. I've always wanted to get really good at taking pictures. That's still a work in progress. In the meantime this is where the pictures live, along with everything else I can't stop talking about.

The rolls

Photos, by the
roll they came off

Four film series and one digital one. Concerts are the reason the camera exists. Everything else is what happened between shows.

5 series  ·  164 frames
Roll 01  ·  69 framesKodak Portra 800 · Kodak T-MAX 3200

Concerts

Small rooms, big lights. Stage color pushed through Portra 800, and T-MAX 3200 when the room gets too dark to care about grain. Plus a band that set up by the lake in Central Park one afternoon.

Open the roll
Roll 02  ·  42 framesArista EDU Ultra 400

Travel

Out West mostly: Garden of the Gods, Red Rocks, the Tetons in October, a dog by every river. Then a detour through London and Ghent.

Open the roll
Roll 03  ·  23 framesKodak Ultra Max 400

New York City

Citi Field, Coney Island, the Manhattan Bridge at golden hour, the elevated tracks in Queens. Ultra Max 400 because the city already has enough contrast.

Open the roll
Roll 04  ·  12 frames35mm

Worn on Tour

Walking up to strangers around New York City who are wearing great band merch and asking to take their picture. Awkward every time. Worth it every time.

Open the roll
Roll 05  ·  18 framesDigital

Sports

Knicks fans in the street during the playoff run, and Argentina supporters turning a stadium parking lot into a party. Shot digital, because you cannot ask a crowd to hold still for film.

Open the roll
Portrait project  ·  @worn.on.tour

Worn on Tourband tees, on film, on strangers

It can be a tad uncomfortable to walk up to random people and ask to take a picture of them. So far it's been worth the awkwardness.

A portrait project that combines the two hobbies: music and photography. Portraits, on film, of people around New York City wearing cool band merchandise. Neil Young tank tops, Smiths tees, Dead shirts that have clearly been to a lot of shows.

Reviewed

Things I love,
on a five-star scale

Borrowed from John Green's The Anthropocene Reviewed, and from a year-end newsletter where I rated the year on a five-star scale. Not self-help. Just a bit of fun.

Scale: ★ to ★★★★★

ReviewedGoing to concerts

★★★★★

Goose six times, Parcels, Luke Bryan, a bluegrass band at Sunny's in Red Hook, and rooms as small as Pete's Candy Store. The full concert experience.

I give going to concerts five stars.

ReviewedBurritos

★★★★★

Officially my favorite food. Rating every new spot across four boroughs. Scrolling Reddit and Google Maps for the next one is one of my most relaxing activities.

I give burritos five stars.

ReviewedShooting film

★★★★★

Thirty-six chances per roll, and you don't find out for two weeks. Somehow that's the appeal.

I give shooting film five stars.

ReviewedCheap beer

★★★★★

Reformed IPA snob with 370+ Untappd check-ins. Turns out the point was always sharing a round with people.

I give cheap beer four stars.

ReviewedNew running shoes

★★★★★

Like a car fresh off a tune-up. Gotta look good to feel good.

I give new running shoes five stars.

ReviewedFeeling uncomfortable

★★★★★

Concerts alone, new jobs, asking strangers for a portrait. It never really goes away. You just stop letting it decide.

I give feeling uncomfortable three stars.

ReviewedImposter syndrome

★★★★★

If the main thing I don't like about my job is that I feel like I don't deserve it, I'm probably in the right room.

I give imposter syndrome two stars.

ReviewedAnora

★★★★★

Best movie I watched last year. They absolutely nailed the ending.

I give Anora five stars.

Venue bucket list

Rooms worth
traveling for

Venues worth traveling for. Underrated places, something funky about the room, music I actually like, and logistics that won't ruin it for an anxious person.

1 / 8 checked off

  1. Red Rocks Amphitheatre

    Morrison, CO

    There are Red Rocks frames in the Travel roll, so we're counting it.

    Been

  2. The Gorge Amphitheatre

    Quincy, WA

    Labor Dave Weekend. As a fellow Dave with a Labor Day birthday, this is destiny.

    Not yet

  3. Codfish Hollow Barnstormers

    Maquoketa, IA

    A 600-cap barn in rural Iowa. What other reason would I have to go to Iowa?

    Not yet

  4. Thekla

    Bristol, UK

    A 1950s German cargo ship you see a show inside of.

    Not yet

  5. Paradiso

    Amsterdam, NL

    An 1880 church. The Stones played it in '95.

    Not yet

  6. Johnny Brenda's

    Philadelphia, PA

    Tiny Fishtown dive, shows upstairs. If I'm going to Philly, I'm going here.

    Not yet

  7. SPAC

    Saratoga Springs, NY

    Was in town. It was Christian-rock weekend. Missed Phish by three weeks.

    Not yet

  8. Sphere

    Las Vegas, NV

    A planetarium for hippies.
